intro: Kvam is a municipality on the north side of the Hardangerfjord in Vestland, western Norway, a place of orchards, steep wooded slopes and small settlements along the water. At Tolo, near the fjord road, stands a low oak whose great mossy limbs leave one short base almost at ground level and lean out in every direction. A reader sent us its photograph and puts it at more than a thousand years old.

trees.name: The Old Oak at Tolo
trees.age_estimate: more than 1,000 years, by a reader's estimate
trees.story:
A reader sent this oak from Tolo in Kvam, on the Hardangerfjord in western Norway, with a GPS fix taken beside it near the fjord road, and gave it an age of more than a thousand years.

The photograph shows an oak that has spent its life spreading rather than climbing. From one short, broad base, four or five great limbs leave the trunk almost at ground level and lean out in every direction, twisting as they go, their grey bark dark with moss. In the middle of them stands a sawn stump, where another limb once was. The crown is thin and green, and between the trunks the water of the fjord shows pale through the trees.

The age is the reader's estimate, and no register we hold lists this tree, so read it as theirs. We have no girth or height for it either, and the photograph does not settle which oak it is, so this page names the genus. If you know its history or have measured it, tell us here.

Look for the cluster of leaning, mossy limbs on the slope above the water.
